text: How well does your assistant know your code? Without a map, it searches, opens file after file, and guesses.
Sensei’s code map opens on modules, not on thousands of symbols. Go down a level when you choose: a module’s files, then a file’s functions and who calls them.
It shows what the code hides: layers called the wrong way round, cycles, and files that always change together with nothing linking them.
Docs are checked against the live code. When a method is renamed, the README that still names it is flagged.
Your assistant can ask Sensei directly, and get the right files, callers, rules and memories on the first turn. When Sensei can’t help, it says so.
And each chunk of work starts at intake. Sensei reads what kind of work it is and how risky, then recommends a way of working. You confirm.
Sensei. Know the code before you change it.
